rows.medi_said: So elsaa el awal

rows.medi_said: and التاني الساعة means a different hour.
rows.amal_said: لا. We can't say تاني الساعة. It doesn't mean anything.

rows.proposed_rule: Before the noun, awal / tani / aa5er / 8eir take no el- (awal sa3a, tani yoam, 8eir yoam); 'the first X' puts the ordinal AFTER as an adjective with el- on both (el-saa3a el-oowla) - el-awal el-saa3a / tani el-saa3a mean nothing
rows.r3_challenge: At 21:50 he is stating a hypothesis about the rule ('if it's the same rule... التاني الساعة means a different hour') - a rule question, not a use; Amal's 'we can't say تاني الساعة' answers the rule question.

rows.medi_said: تاني حاجة.
rows.amal_said: تاني حدا would mean the second person.
rows.why: Engine wrote حاجة; Amal echoes تاني حدا - before the noun tani means 'second', for 'someone else' it goes after: 7ada taani.
rows.proposed_rule: Tool words awal / aa5er / tani / 8eir: right BEFORE a noun they take the bare noun with no el- (tani 7ada = second person, 8eir yoam = another day, aa5er muwazzafe = the last employee); awal el- / aa5er el- + noun means beginning / end of; AFTER the noun they act as adjectives (7ada taani = someone else)
